correctness.rationale: The graph has exactly twelve edges across three opposite vertex-pairs; a face is any selected edge set with degree <=2 at every graph vertex, equivalently avoiding each incident edge triple. An independent exact enumeration found 772 faces including the empty face. A sequential twelve-edge toggle matching has 378 pairs, sixteen critical faces (six in dimension three, ten in four) and an acyclic orientation over all 2940 Hasse incidences. Independently implemented generic integral unit-pivot Schur cancellations of all pairs, obtaining a 6x10 Morse d4 with rank three and Smith factors (1,1,1), hence H3=Z^3 and H4=Z^7 without torsion. Since the resulting CW complex has only 0-,3-,4-cells and pi3 of its 3-skeleton is Z^6, primitive attaching degrees can be diagonalized/cancelled to give the claimed wedge. No homotopy conclusion is inferred from mod-two Betti numbers alone.
residual_risks: Exact finite graph classification only, not a formula for arbitrary complete multipartite graphs.

value.rationale: The regular octahedral graph is a basic Platonic graph and the first small canonical complete tripartite example outside commonly computed K_n/K_{p,q} two-matching families. Its nonpure complex surprisingly has a torsion-free mixed-dimensional integral wedge; a complete homotopy type, rather than just Betti numbers, supplies a meaningful benchmark and boundary case for higher matching-complex classifications.
residual_risks: One isolated small graph is less general than a structural family theorem, so the mathematical value lies in its natural graph/invariant and exact mixed-dimensional boundary witness.
